newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hongkong Electric to expand outside HK.
newsitem.headline: Hongkong Electric to expand outside HK.

text.p: Hongkong Electric Holdings Ltd has set up a new subsidiary to pursue growth opportunities outside Hong Kong, the company said on Thursday.
"The reorganisation paves the way for our group to actively pursue investment opportunities outside Hong Kong through Hongkong Electric International Ltd," a company statement said.

A reorganisation of the Cheung Kong Holdings Ltd group announced in January 1997, proposed that the controlling shareholder of Hongkong Electric be changed to Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd from Hutchison Whampoa Ltd .
The statement gave no details on potential projects to be undertaken by the new company.
The company made the announcement in a statement accompanying its 1996 earnings results.

Hongkong Electric reported net profit of HK$4.15 billion, a decline of 0.8 percent over 1995. Earnings per share declined to HK$2.06 from HK$2.07, while dividends rose to HK$1.23 per share from HK$1.11, an increase of 10.8 percent.

The decline in net profit was due to the substantial decline in profits from an associate company involved in the redeveloment of one of the utility company's former power station sites, the statement said.
However, the core business continued to show a satisfactory profit growth of 11.7 percent over the previous year, it said.

"Following a lackluste first six months in electricity sales, the weather improved for the remainder of the year and demand picked up strongly with unit sales of electricity increasing by 10.3 percent in the last quarter," it said. "Total unit sales rose by 5.9 percent as compared with 1995."
In January 1997, the electricity company increased its net average tariff by HK$0.029 per kilowatt hour, an increase of 3.47 percent.
"Our average annual tariff increase over this period of 14 years was 2.6 percent compared to inflation of 7.6 percent per annum," the statement said.
Looking ahead, the company said its investment programme was on schedule and a new 350 MW generating unit, the eighth to be installed in its Lamma plant, would be commissioned at the end of 1997.
The utility was also continuing discussions with the government on its generating capacity needs to meet demand by the year 2003, it said.
